items.title: Anthropic IPO raises over $81 billion in largest offering on record, topping SpaceX
items.summary: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share, above its targeted range, raising more than $81 billion in the largest public offering on record and surpassing SpaceX. The Claude maker's shares were set to begin trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, with the sale valuing the company at more than $1.5 trillion.
items.why_it_matters: It is the first frontier AI lab to go public, a landmark test of how public markets value the AI boom.

items.title: How Nvidia Chips Ended Up Within Reach of China’s Military
items.summary: A New York Times investigation found that Alibaba, the Chinese tech giant at the center of the Nvidia espionage affair that led to Jensen Huang's resignation, used Nvidia AI computing technology to aid a lab with links to China's military. Separately, Jensen Huang has agreed to testify before the Senate banking committee about the matter.
items.why_it_matters: It raises fresh national-security questions about whether US export controls on AI chips are actually working.

items.title: A.I. Makes More Tech Outages Likely, Microsoft’s Chief Warns
items.summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said AI tools are now finding cybersecurity bugs so quickly that companies must deploy fixes almost instantaneously, which he said is contributing to a recent wave of tech outages. He separately called much of the world's critical infrastructure "unpatchable."
items.why_it_matters: It is a rare admission from a top tech executive that AI-accelerated patching is itself becoming a source of real-world instability.

items.title: Palo Alto Networks to Buy AI-Startup Applied Compute for $4.5 Billion
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks agreed to buy Applied Compute, a startup founded last year by former OpenAI researchers that specializes in customizing open-weight AI models, for $4.5 billion.
items.why_it_matters: It shows cybersecurity vendors racing to buy their way into AI model customization as a core competitive capability.

items.title: NYC, LA and Chicago School Districts Weigh Breaking Up With Google Search Over A.I.
items.summary: New York, Los Angeles and Chicago school districts are considering dropping Google Search after Google said schools will no longer be able to disable its Gemini-powered AI features without also disabling Search entirely, starting next year.
items.why_it_matters: It is a concrete example of institutions pushing back against forced AI bundling in widely used products.

items.title: Microsoft Says Copilot Is Beating Anthropic, OpenAI on Price
items.summary: Microsoft said customers are increasingly choosing its Copilot AI assistant over Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's ChatGPT because Copilot is cheaper to operate.
items.why_it_matters: It signals that price, not just capability, is becoming a key battleground among the leading AI assistants.

items.title: JPMorgan is working on AI agent transactions that don’t involve humans
items.summary: JPMorgan and Hyundai Card are working to expand the use of AI agents that can carry out financial transactions without human involvement.
items.why_it_matters: Autonomous agent-to-agent payments would be a significant shift in how money moves through the financial system.

items.title: AI asked ‘better questions’ than KPMG accountants in pilot audit
items.summary: A Big Four firm, KPMG, used AI agents to review the financial statements of a FTSE 250 company in a pilot audit, with the agents reportedly asking better questions than human accountants, though human intervention was still needed.
items.why_it_matters: It is an early, concrete data point on AI agents performing above human baselines in a high-stakes professional task.

items.title: US, Malaysia To Strengthen Sovereign AI Cloud Development
items.summary: The US and Malaysia plan to cooperate on building out Malaysia's sovereign AI cloud, with Washington offering $50 million in support.
items.why_it_matters: It's another sign of governments racing to secure their own AI compute infrastructure rather than relying solely on US hyperscalers.

items.title: Energy-Based Reasoners: 385x more efficient inference
items.summary: A research project called Energy-Based Reasoners claims a new reasoning/inference technique that is up to 385x more efficient than existing approaches. The project drew significant attention on Hacker News, with 273 points and 44 comments.
items.why_it_matters: Large efficiency gains in inference, if they hold up, would meaningfully lower the cost of running reasoning models at scale.

items.title: Snapchat now lets developers build AR Lenses with AI assistants like Claude Code and Cursor
items.summary: Snapchat now lets Lens creators describe the AR Lens they want in plain language, with AI coding assistants such as Claude Code and Cursor handling the build process from start to finish.
items.why_it_matters: It's a concrete example of AI coding agents being embedded directly into a consumer platform's creator tools.

items.title: [AINews] GPT-6.2 Astra, the #2 Frontier Model is better and 20%-600% cheaper, but has mixed reviews; 6.2 Sol likely main workhorse
items.summary: Early testers of OpenAI's newly launched GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol models report lower benchmark costs, with pricing 20% to 600% cheaper than prior models, but reviews on Astra's real-world usability are mixed, while Sol is emerging as the likely default workhorse model.
items.why_it_matters: First independent reactions to a new frontier model often reveal gaps between benchmark performance and practical usability.

items.title: City firms told to tighten cyber defences as AI exposes vulnerabilities
items.summary: Regulators published new guidance directing City of London financial firms to tighten their cyber defences, following a surge in hacking attempts and a $6 billion theft from the crypto exchange Binance, amid growing concern that AI is exposing new vulnerabilities.
items.why_it_matters: It shows financial regulators moving to respond to AI-era security risks with concrete new requirements.
